walkthroughs.body_html:
Exponentials & Logarithms — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Exponentials & Logarithms brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Exponentials & Logarithms.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: When solving 3x = 12, what do you do to both sides?
options: Divide both sides by 3 to get x = 4.
There are infinitely many roots.
Subtract 3 from both sides because 3 was multiplying x.
Multiply both sides by 3 to undo the equation.

mcqs.q: If the discriminant of a quadratic is negative, what does it tell you about real roots?
options: There are no real roots — the graph does not cross the x-axis.
Multiply both sides by 3 to undo the equation.
There is one repeated root — the curve just touches the x-axis.
There are infinitely many roots.

mcqs.q: Which average is best to use for the data set [2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 100]?
options: The mean — it always gives the most accurate average.
The median (3.5) — it isn't distorted by the outlier 100, unlike the mean.
There are infinitely many roots.
The mode, because the most common value is always the best representative.
